title: Metric-driven automated gating and selection for multilingual reranker upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: introduce an automated, metric-driven gating system for selecting cross-encoder variants during staged reranker upgrades across languages and traffic tiers. This ticket coordinates offline evaluation, canary gating, and automated rollback triggers so we can safely ship higher-quality cross-encoder variants without manual per-locale intervention.

Background: We have multiple candidate cross-encoder families (compact, base, hybrid-symmetric) plus quantized variants. Past rollouts required manual selection and ad-hoc smoke checks which slowed upgrades and increased regression risk in low-volume locales. We need a reproducible pipeline that 1) ranks candidates per workload by a composed score (quality uplift vs latency/cost), 2) defines deterministic pass/fail gates for canary and ramp, and 3) automates rollback or fall-through to fallback variants.

Success criteria (must be measured and enforced by gates):
- Offline: NDCG@10 uplift >= 1.2% vs current baseline on evaluation suites aggregated across top 20 locales (per-locale floor >= 0.5%).
- Online canary: No regression in user CTR surrogate metric (p-value>0.05 for uplift) and client-visible latency p95 change <= +10ms in the canary slice.
- Latency budget: end-to-end rerank P50 <= 20ms and P95 <= 60ms for top-100 candidate re-ranks in hosted mode on typical request shapes.
- Cost: per-request inference cost delta <= +15% for material quality gains (team will accept up to +25% if quality > 2.5%).

Approach:
1) Offline evaluation harness extension
   - Build per-locale evaluation runs for each candidate using existing regression harness. Include shuffled prompt seeds, stratified by sequence-length and candidate-pool-size.
   - Compute: NDCG@k, MAP, latency distribution (simulated with hardware profiles), and token-cost estimate.
   - Output: single scalar "composed_score" = alpha * normalized_quality - beta * normalized_latency - gamma * normalized_cost, where alpha/beta/gamma are tunable in the Console experiment config (default alpha=0.7, beta=0.2, gamma=0.1).

2) Automated gating service (new small component)
   - Input: offline composed_score table + historical production latency profiles + experiment config (thresholds per-customer-tier and per-locale).
   - Output: "approved_candidates" for staged rollout with reason codes and confidence intervals.
   - Exposes REST endpoints used by rollout orchestrator to provision canaries.

3) Canary and progressive ramp policy
   - Canary slice: 0.5% of traffic per locale (or regional aggregator for low-volume locales).
   - Gate checks at 24h and 72h: statistical tests on quality proxy, latency SLOs, error rates, and cost deltas.
   - If gate fails for a locale, automatically fall back to the previous model version and mark candidate as failed for that locale.

4) Regression and monitoring
   - Add per-candidate, per-locale dashboards in Console with NDCG, latency p50/p95, error rates, and cost per request.
   - Hook alerts for: quality regression > -0.5% absolute on primary metric OR latency p95 increase > +25ms OR error-rate spike > 3x baseline. Alerts create P0 incident and trigger automatic rollback.

5) Fallback strategies
   - Graceful degradation: for latency violations use hybrid flow: bi-encoder candidate retrieval -> lightweight cross-encoder (quantized) re-rank for top-50. This keeps p95 bounded while preserving most quality gains.
   - For memory-constrained dedicated pools, fall back to quantized base variant and adjust batch sizing automatically.

Datasets and artifacts:
- Eval suites: top20_locales_eval_v3 (Drive link placeholder: https://drive.redwood.ai/evals/top20_v3)
- Benchmark harness: github.com/redwood-inference/rr-bench (PRs and results stored under /results/rerank/ENG-21421)
- Experiment configs stored in Console under "rerank/gating/ENG-21421".

Rollout plan and milestones:
- Spike (DONE): offline harness changes + composed_score prototype (Aisha) - created 2025-03-05.
- Benchmarks (IN PROGRESS): run hybrid-symmetric, compact-quantized variants on top20 suite across hardware profiles (Luca) - target complete 2025-03-12.
- Gating service (BLOCKED -> In Progress): implement REST service + store candidate decisions (blocked on infra quota for dedicated canary pools).
- Canary (Planned): deploy approved candidate to 0.5% traffic, monitor 72h, auto-decide.
- Ramp and cleanup (Planned): ramp to 25% then 100% with progressive checks.

Acceptance criteria for DONE:
- Gating service runs end-to-end: inputs offline scores, outputs approved candidate list.
- Canary orchestration triggers based on approval and completes 72h checks automatically (or records deterministic failure reason).
- No detected production regressions during canary on primary locales for 7 consecutive days.
- Documentation and runbook added to Confluence: "Reranker upgrade automation" with rollback steps and owner list.

Open decisions / trade-offs:
- Threshold definitions: default alpha/beta/gamma tuning above are provisional; PM and Research must sign off.
- Per-locale sample sizes: low-volume locales may require regional aggregation or looser statistical power; acceptance policy needed.
- Cost vs quality budget: product to decide acceptable max delta per release.

Risks:
- Overfitting to offline eval sets leading to false positives in gating. Mitigation: add holdout online probes and user-level proxies.
- Infra constraints for canaries on dedicated pools. Mitigation: use hosted canary + synthetic traffic for some checks.
